passages.text: After this, Jesus crossed to the other side of the Sea of Galilee (that is, the Sea of Tiberias).
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus finished speaking to the people.
Jesus left the place where He was.
Jesus crossed to the other side of the Sea of Galilee.
The Sea of Galilee is also called the Sea of Tiberias.
passages.original: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἀπῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης τῆς Γαλιλαίας τῆς Τιβεριάδος

passages.text: A large crowd followed Him because they saw the signs He was performing on the sick.
passages.sermon:
Jesus traveled in Galilee.
A large crowd followed Jesus.
The people saw Jesus perform signs.
Jesus healed sick people.
The crowd followed because they saw these signs.
passages.original: ἠκολούθει δὲ αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς ὅτι ἐθεώρουν τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐποίει ἐπὶ τῶν ἀσθενούντων

passages.text: Then Jesus went up on the mountain and sat down with His disciples.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus went up on the mountain.
His disciples followed Him.
Jesus sat down with His disciples on the mountain.
passages.original: ἀνῆλθεν δὲ εἰς τὸ ὄρος Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἐκεῖ ἐκάθητο μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Now the Jewish Feast of the Passover was near.
passages.sermon: The Jewish Feast of the Passover was near.\r\nThis feast was important to the Jews.\r\nThe time was close to this celebration.
passages.original: Ἦν δὲ ἐγγὺς τὸ πάσχα ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων

passages.text: When Jesus looked up and saw a large crowd coming toward Him, He said to Philip, “Where can we buy bread for these people to eat?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was sitting on the mountain with His disciples.
He looked up.
He saw a large crowd coming toward Him.
Jesus spoke to Philip.
He asked Philip a question.
Jesus said, “Where can we buy bread for these people to eat?”
passages.original: ἐπάρας οὖν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ θεασάμενος ὅτι πολὺς ὄχλος ἔρχεται πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγει πρὸς Φίλιππον Πόθεν ἀγοράσωμεν ἄρτους ἵνα φάγωσιν οὗτοι

passages.text: But He was asking this to test him, for He knew what He was about to do.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to Philip.\r\nJesus wanted to test Philip.\r\nJesus already knew what He was going to do.
passages.original: τοῦτο δὲ ἔλεγεν πειράζων αὐτόν αὐτὸς γὰρ ᾔδει τί ἔμελλεν ποιεῖν

passages.text: Philip answered, “Two hundred denarii would not buy enough bread for each of them to have a small piece.”
passages.sermon:
Philip was one of Jesus’ disciples.
A large crowd was coming to Jesus.
Jesus asked Philip where they could buy bread for the people.
Philip answered Jesus.
He said, “Two hundred denarii would not buy enough bread.”
He meant that even with two hundred denarii, there would not be enough bread.
Each person would only get a small piece.
The money was not enough for everyone.
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ ὁ Φίλιππος Διακοσίων δηναρίων ἄρτοι οὐκ ἀρκοῦσιν αὐτοῖς ἵνα ἕκαστος βραχύ τι λάβῃ

passages.text: One of His disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to Him, “Here is a boy with five barley loaves and two small fish. But what difference will these make among so many?”
passages.sermon:
Andrew was one of Jesus’ disciples.
Andrew was Simon Peter’s brother.
Andrew spoke to Jesus.
Andrew said, “There is a boy here.”
The boy has five barley loaves.
The boy also has two small fish.
Andrew said, “But what are these for so many people?”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ εἷς ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς Σίμωνος Πέτρου Ἔστιν παιδάριον ὧδε ὃς ἔχει πέντε ἄρτους κριθίνους καὶ δύο ὀψάρια ἀλλὰ ταῦτα τί ἐστιν εἰς τοσούτους

passages.text: “Have the people sit down,” Jesus said. Now there was plenty of grass in that place, so the men sat down, about five thousand of them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus told them to have the people sit down.
There was a lot of grass in that place.
The men sat down.
About five thousand men sat down.
passages.original: Εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ποιήσατε τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἀναπεσεῖν ἦν δὲ χόρτος πολὺς ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ἀνέπεσαν οὖν οἱ ἄνδρες τὸν ἀριθμὸν ὡς πεντακισχίλιοι

passages.text: Then Jesus took the loaves and the fish, gave thanks, and distributed to those who were seated as much as they wanted.
passages.sermon:
Jesus took the loaves.
Jesus took the fish.
Jesus gave thanks.
Jesus gave the loaves to the people who were sitting down.
Jesus gave the fish to the people who were sitting down.
The people took as much as they wanted.
passages.original: Ἔλαβεν οὖν τοὺς ἄρτους ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ εὐχαριστήσας διέδωκεν τοῖς ἀνακειμένοις ὁμοίως καὶ ἐκ τῶν ὀψαρίων ὅσον ἤθελον

passages.text: And when everyone was full, He said to His disciples, “Gather the pieces that are left over, so that nothing will be wasted.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
\r\nJesus performed a miracle and fed about five thousand men.
\r\nEveryone ate until they were full.
\r\nJesus spoke to His disciples.
\r\nHe told them, “Gather the pieces that are left over.”
\r\nHe said this so that nothing would be wasted.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐνεπλήσθησαν λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ Συναγάγετε τὰ περισσεύσαντα κλάσματα ἵνα μή τι ἀπόληται

passages.text: So they collected them and filled twelve baskets with the pieces of the five barley loaves left over by those who had eaten.
passages.sermon:
The disciples collected the leftover pieces.
They gathered the pieces from the five barley loaves.
These pieces were left over after everyone had eaten.
They filled twelve baskets with the leftover pieces.
passages.original: συνήγαγον οὖν καὶ ἐγέμισαν δώδεκα κοφίνους κλασμάτων ἐκ τῶν πέντε ἄρτων τῶν κριθίνων ἃ ἐπερίσσευσαν τοῖς βεβρωκόσιν

passages.text: When the people saw the sign that Jesus had performed, they began to say, “Truly this is the Prophet who is to come into the world.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus performed a sign.
People saw what Jesus did.
The people spoke to each other.
They said, “This man is truly the Prophet.”
They said, “He is the one who is coming into the world.”
passages.original: Οἱ οὖν ἄνθρωποι ἰδόντες ὃ ἐποίησεν σημεῖον ἔλεγον ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν ἀληθῶς ὁ προφήτης ὁ ἐρχόμενος εἰς τὸν κόσμον

passages.text: Then Jesus, realizing that they were about to come and make Him king by force, withdrew again to a mountain by Himself.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus performed a miracle.
The people saw the miracle.
The people wanted to make Jesus their king by force.
Jesus realized their intention.
Jesus withdrew.
He went again to a mountain.
Jesus went alone.
passages.original: Ἰησοῦς οὖν γνοὺς ὅτι μέλλουσιν ἔρχεσθαι καὶ ἁρπάζειν αὐτὸν ἵνα ποιήσωσιν βασιλέα ἀνεχώρησεν πάλιν εἰς τὸ ὄρος αὐτὸς μόνος

passages.text: When evening came, His disciples went down to the sea, got into a boat, and started across the sea to Capernaum. It was already dark, and Jesus had not yet gone out to them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had disciples.
Evening came.
The disciples went down to the sea.
They got into a boat.
They started to cross the sea.
They were going to Capernaum.
It was already dark.
Jesus had not yet gone out to them.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ὀψία ἐγένετο κατέβησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ ἐμβάντες εἰς πλοῖον ἤρχοντο πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἰς Καφαρναούμ καὶ σκοτία ἤδη ἐγεγόνει καὶ οὔπω ἐληλύθει πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς

passages.text: A strong wind was blowing, and the sea grew agitated.
passages.sermon: A strong wind blew.\r\nThe sea became rough.
passages.original: ἥ τε θάλασσα ἀνέμου μεγάλου πνέοντος διεγείρετο

passages.text: When they had rowed about three or four miles, they saw Jesus approaching the boat, walking on the sea—and they were terrified.
passages.sermon:
The disciples rowed the boat for about three or four miles.
They saw Jesus.
Jesus was walking on the sea.
Jesus came near the boat.
The disciples became terrified.
passages.original: Ἐληλακότες οὖν ὡς σταδίους εἴκοσι πέντε ἢ τριάκοντα θεωροῦσιν τὸν Ἰησοῦν περιπατοῦντα ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἐγγὺς τοῦ πλοίου γινόμενον καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν

passages.text: But Jesus spoke up: “It is I; do not be afraid.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to them.\r\nHe said, "It is I."\r\nHe said, "Do not be afraid."
passages.original: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἐγώ εἰμι μὴ φοβεῖσθε

passages.text: Then they were willing to take Him into the boat, and at once the boat reached the shore where they were heading.
passages.sermon:
The disciples saw Jesus walking on the sea.
They became willing to take Jesus into the boat.
Immediately, the boat reached the shore.
The boat arrived at the place where the disciples were going.
passages.original: ἤθελον οὖν λαβεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον καὶ εὐθέως ἐγένετο τὸ πλοῖον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς εἰς ἣν ὑπῆγον

passages.text: The next day, the crowd that had remained on the other side of the sea realized that only one boat had been there, and that Jesus had not boarded it with His disciples, but they had gone away alone.
passages.sermon:
The crowd stood on the other side of the sea.
This happened the next day.
They saw only one boat there.
They realized Jesus had not entered the boat with His disciples.
They saw that only His disciples had left in the boat.
Jesus did not go with them.
passages.original: Τῇ ἐπαύριον ὁ ὄχλος ὁ ἑστηκὼς πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἶδον ὅτι πλοιάριον ἄλλο οὐκ ἦν ἐκεῖ εἰ μὴ ἕν καὶ ὅτι οὐ συνεισῆλθεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ πλοῖον ἀλλὰ μόνοι οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἀπῆλθον

passages.text: However, some boats from Tiberias landed near the place where the people had eaten the bread after the Lord had given thanks.
passages.sermon: Some boats came from Tiberias.\r\nThese boats arrived near the place where the people had eaten bread.\r\nThe Lord had given thanks before the people ate the bread.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ἦλθεν πλοιάρια ἐκ Τιβεριάδος ἐγγὺς τοῦ τόπου ὅπου ἔφαγον τὸν ἄρτον εὐχαριστήσαντος τοῦ Κυρίου

passages.text: So when the crowd saw that neither Jesus nor His disciples were there, they got into the boats and went to Capernaum to look for Him.
passages.sermon:
A crowd stood on the other side of the sea.
They looked for Jesus.
They did not see Jesus there.
They did not see His disciples there.
The crowd realized Jesus and His disciples were both gone.
The crowd got into the boats.
They went to Capernaum.
They wanted to find Jesus.
passages.original: ὅτε οὖν εἶδεν ὁ ὄχλος ὅτι Ἰησοῦς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκεῖ οὐδὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἐνέβησαν αὐτοὶ εἰς τὰ πλοιάρια καὶ ἦλθον εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ ζητοῦντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: When they found Him on the other side of the sea, they asked Him, “Rabbi, when did You get here?”
passages.sermon:
A crowd looked for Jesus.
They did not find Him where He had fed them bread.
They got into boats from Tiberias.
They crossed the sea to Capernaum.
They searched for Jesus there.
They found Jesus on the other side of the sea.
They spoke to Him.
They said, “Rabbi, when did You get here?”
passages.original: καὶ εὑρόντες αὐτὸν πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἶπον αὐτῷ Ῥαββί πότε ὧδε γέγονας

passages.text: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it is not because you saw these signs that you are looking for Me, but because you ate the loaves and had your fill.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowd.
He answered them directly.
He said, “Truly, truly, I tell you this.
You are looking for Me.
You do not seek Me because you saw signs.
You seek Me because you ate the bread.
You were satisfied by the food.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ζητεῖτέ με οὐχ ὅτι εἴδετε σημεῖα ἀλλ’ ὅτι ἐφάγετε ἐκ τῶν ἄρτων καὶ ἐχορτάσθητε

passages.text: Do not work for food that perishes, but for food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For on Him God the Father has placed His seal of approval.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus is the Son of Man.
God the Father has given His seal of approval to Jesus.
Jesus told them not to work for food that spoils.
He told them to work for food that lasts forever.
This food gives eternal life.
The Son of Man, Jesus, will give this food to them.
passages.original: ἐργάζεσθε μὴ τὴν βρῶσιν τὴν ἀπολλυμένην ἀλλὰ τὴν βρῶσιν τὴν μένουσαν εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον ἣν ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὑμῖν δώσει τοῦτον γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ ἐσφράγισεν ὁ Θεός

passages.text: Then they inquired, “What must we do to perform the works of God?”
passages.sermon:
The people spoke to Jesus.
They asked Him a question.
They said, "What must we do?"
They wanted to know how to do the works of God.
They asked, "How can we do what God wants?"
passages.original: Εἶπον οὖν πρὸς αὐτόν Τί ποιῶμεν ἵνα ἐργαζώμεθα τὰ ἔργα τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Jesus replied, “The work of God is this: to believe in the One He has sent.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus answered their question.
Jesus explained the work of God.
God wants you to believe in the One He has sent.
God sent this One to you.
Believing in Him is the work God desires.
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ ἔργον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἵνα πιστεύητε εἰς ὃν ἀπέστειλεν ἐκεῖνος

passages.text: So they asked Him, “What sign then will You perform, so that we may see it and believe You? What will You do?
passages.sermon:
The people spoke to Jesus.
They asked Him a question.
They said, “What sign will you do?”
They wanted to see a sign.
They wanted to believe Him.
They also asked, “What will you do?”
passages.original: Εἶπον οὖν αὐτῷ Τί οὖν ποιεῖς σὺ σημεῖον ἵνα ἴδωμεν καὶ πιστεύσωμέν σοι τί ἐργάζῃ

passages.text: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, as it is written: ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’”
passages.sermon:
Our ancestors lived long ago.
They traveled in the wilderness.
God gave them manna to eat.
Manna was bread from heaven.
Scripture says, “He gave them bread from heaven to eat.”
passages.original: οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν τὸ μάννα ἔφαγον ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ καθώς ἐστιν γεγραμμένον Ἄρτον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς φαγεῖν

passages.text: Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven, but it is My Father who gives you the true bread from heaven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said, "I tell you the truth."
Moses did not give you the bread from heaven.
My Father gives you the true bread from heaven.
passages.original: Εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν οὐ Μωϋσῆς δέδωκεν ὑμῖν τὸν ἄρτον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀλλ’ ὁ Πατήρ μου δίδωσιν ὑμῖν τὸν ἄρτον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ τὸν ἀληθινόν

passages.text: For the bread of God is He who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.”
passages.sermon: The bread of God is a person.\r\nThis person comes down from heaven.\r\nHe gives life to the world.
passages.original: ὁ γὰρ ἄρτος τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστιν ὁ καταβαίνων ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ζωὴν διδοὺς τῷ κόσμῳ

passages.text: “Sir,” they said, “give us this bread at all times.”
passages.sermon:
The people spoke to Jesus.
They called Him “Sir.”
They asked Jesus for bread.
They said, “Give us this bread.”
They wanted this bread always.
They asked for this bread at all times.
passages.original: Εἶπον οὖν πρὸς αὐτόν Κύριε πάντοτε δὸς ἡμῖν τὸν ἄρτον τοῦτον

passages.text: Jesus answered, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to Me will never hunger, and whoever believes in Me will never thirst.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus is the bread of life.
Anyone who comes to Jesus will never be hungry.
Anyone who believes in Jesus will never be thirsty.
passages.original: Εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος τῆς ζωῆς ὁ ἐρχόμενος πρὸς ἐμὲ οὐ μὴ πεινάσῃ καὶ ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ μὴ διψήσει πώποτε

passages.text: But as I stated, you have seen Me and still you do not believe.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the people.\r\nJesus said, “You have seen Me.\r\nBut you do not believe in Me.”
passages.original: ἀλλ’ εἶπον ὑμῖν ὅτι καὶ ἑωράκατέ με καὶ οὐ πιστεύετε

passages.text: Everyone the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will never drive away.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus is the Son of God.
God the Father gives people to Jesus.
Every person the Father gives to Jesus will come to Jesus.
Anyone who comes to Jesus, Jesus will never reject.
passages.original: Πᾶν ὃ δίδωσίν μοι ὁ Πατὴρ πρὸς ἐμὲ ἥξει καὶ τὸν ἐρχόμενον πρός με οὐ μὴ ἐκβάλω ἔξω

passages.text: For I have come down from heaven, not to do My own will, but to do the will of Him who sent Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus came down from heaven.
Jesus did not come to do His own will.
Jesus came to do the will of the One who sent Him.
God the Father sent Jesus.
passages.original: ὅτι καταβέβηκα ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ οὐχ ἵνα ποιῶ τὸ θέλημα τὸ ἐμὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με

passages.text: And this is the will of Him who sent Me, that I shall lose none of those He has given Me, but raise them up at the last day.
passages.sermon:
God the Father sent Me.
God gave certain people to Me.
God wants Me to keep every person He gave Me.
I will not lose any of them.
I will raise each one up on the last day.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δέ ἐστιν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με ἵνα πᾶν ὃ δέδωκέν μοι μὴ ἀπολέσω ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸ ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ

passages.text: For it is My Father’s will that everyone who looks to the Son and believes in Him shall have eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.”
passages.sermon:
God is my Father.
God has a will.
God wants everyone to look to the Son.
God wants everyone to believe in the Son.
Everyone who looks to the Son and believes in Him will have eternal life.
I will raise that person up at the last day.
passages.original: τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Πατρός μου ἵνα πᾶς ὁ θεωρῶν τὸν Υἱὸν καὶ πιστεύων εἰς αὐτὸν ἔχῃ ζωὴν αἰώνιον καὶ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸν ἐγὼ ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ

passages.text: At this, the Jews began to grumble about Jesus because He had said, “I am the bread that came down from heaven.”
passages.sermon:
The Jews heard Jesus speak.
Jesus said, “I am the bread that came down from heaven.”
The Jews began to grumble about Jesus.
They grumbled because of what Jesus said.
passages.original: Ἐγόγγυζον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι εἶπεν Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος ὁ καταβὰς ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ

passages.text: They were asking, “Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then can He say, ‘I have come down from heaven?’ ”
passages.sermon:
The Jews spoke about Jesus.
They said, “Is this not Jesus?”
Jesus is the son of Joseph.
We know his father.
We know his mother.
How can Jesus say, ‘I have come down from heaven?’”
passages.original: καὶ ἔλεγον Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς ὁ υἱὸς Ἰωσήφ οὗ ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα πῶς νῦν λέγει ὅτι Ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβέβηκα

passages.text: “Stop grumbling among yourselves,” Jesus replied.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the Jews.\r\nHe answered them.\r\nHe said, “Do not grumble among yourselves.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Μὴ γογγύζετε μετ’ ἀλλήλων

passages.text: “No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him, and I will raise him up at the last day.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus is the Son of God.
God the Father sent Jesus.
No one can come to Jesus unless the Father draws that person.
The Father must draw each person to Jesus.
If the Father draws someone, that person comes to Jesus.
Jesus will raise that person up on the last day.
passages.original: οὐδεὶς δύναται ἐλθεῖν πρός με ἐὰν μὴ ὁ Πατὴρ ὁ πέμψας με ἑλκύσῃ αὐτόν κἀγὼ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ

passages.text: It is written in the Prophets: ‘And they will all be taught by God.’ Everyone who has heard the Father and learned from Him comes to Me— not that anyone has seen the Father except the One who is from God; only He has seen the Father.
passages.sermon:
The Prophets wrote these words.
God will teach all people.
Everyone who hears the Father comes to Me.
Everyone who learns from the Father comes to Me.
No one has seen the Father.
Only the One who is from God has seen the Father.
I am the One who is from God.
Only I have seen the Father.
passages.original: ἔστιν γεγραμμένον ἐν τοῖς προφήταις Καὶ ἔσονται πάντες διδακτοὶ Θεοῦ πᾶς ὁ ἀκούσας παρὰ τοῦ Πατρὸς καὶ μαθὼν ἔρχεται πρὸς ἐμέ οὐχ ὅτι τὸν Πατέρα ἑώρακέν τις εἰ μὴ ὁ ὢν παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ οὗτος ἑώρακεν τὸν Πατέρα

passages.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, he who believes has eternal life.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus says something very important.
Jesus says, “Truly, truly, I tell you.”
Anyone who believes has eternal life.
Belief gives eternal life.
passages.original: Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὁ πιστεύων ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον

passages.text: I am the bread of life.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks.
Jesus says, “I am the bread of life.”
Jesus gives life.
Jesus is the source of true life.
passages.original: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος τῆς ζωῆς

passages.text: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, yet they died.
passages.sermon:
Your fathers lived long ago.
They were in the wilderness.
They ate manna there.
They still died.
passages.original: οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν ἔφαγον ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τὸ μάννα καὶ ἀπέθανον

passages.text: This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that anyone may eat of it and not die.
passages.sermon: This bread comes down from heaven.\r\nAnyone may eat this bread.\r\nAnyone who eats this bread will not die.
passages.original: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἄρτος ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβαίνων ἵνα τις ἐξ αὐτοῦ φάγῃ καὶ μὴ ἀποθάνῃ

passages.text: I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. And this bread, which I will give for the life of the world, is My flesh.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus is the living bread.
This living bread came down from heaven.
If anyone eats this bread, that person will live forever.
The bread that Jesus gives is His flesh.
Jesus gives His flesh for the life of the world.
passages.original: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος ὁ ζῶν ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβάς ἐάν τις φάγῃ ἐκ τούτου τοῦ ἄρτου ζήσει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα καὶ ὁ ἄρτος δὲ ὃν ἐγὼ δώσω ἡ σάρξ μού ἐστιν ὑπὲρ τῆς τοῦ κόσμου ζωῆς

passages.text: At this, the Jews began to argue among themselves, “How can this man give us His flesh to eat?”
passages.sermon: The Jews heard Jesus speak.\r\nThey began to argue with each other.\r\nThey said, “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?”
passages.original: Ἐμάχοντο οὖν πρὸς ἀλλήλους οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι λέγοντες Πῶς δύναται οὗτος ἡμῖν δοῦναι τὴν σάρκα αὐτοῦ φαγεῖν

passages.text: So Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, unless you eat the flesh and drink the blood of the Son of Man, you have no life in you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus said, "I tell you the truth."
You must eat the flesh of the Son of Man.
You must drink His blood.
If you do not eat His flesh and drink His blood, you do not have life in yourselves.
passages.original: Εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἐὰν μὴ φάγητε τὴν σάρκα τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ πίητε αὐτοῦ τὸ αἷμα οὐκ ἔχετε ζωὴν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς

passages.text: Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Jews.
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus said, “Whoever eats My flesh has eternal life.”
Jesus said, “Whoever drinks My blood has eternal life.”
I will raise that person up at the last day.
passages.original: ὁ τρώγων μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ πίνων μου τὸ αἷμα ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον κἀγὼ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ

passages.text: For My flesh is real food, and My blood is real drink.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus says, "My flesh is real food."
Jesus says, "My blood is real drink."
passages.original: ἡ γὰρ σάρξ μου ἀληθής ἐστιν βρῶσις καὶ τὸ αἷμά μου ἀληθής ἐστιν πόσις

passages.text: Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood remains in Me, and I in him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke these words while teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus said, “Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood remains in Me.
I also remain in that person.”
passages.original: Ὁ τρώγων μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ πίνων μου τὸ αἷμα ἐν ἐμοὶ μένει κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ

passages.text: Just as the living Father sent Me and I live because of the Father, so also the one who feeds on Me will live because of Me.
passages.sermon:
God is the living Father.
The living Father sent Me.
I am Jesus.
I live because of the Father.
Anyone who feeds on Me will live because of Me.
passages.original: καθὼς ἀπέστειλέν με ὁ ζῶν Πατὴρ κἀγὼ ζῶ διὰ τὸν Πατέρα καὶ ὁ τρώγων με κἀκεῖνος ζήσει δι’ ἐμέ

passages.text: This is the bread that came down from heaven. Unlike your fathers, who ate the manna and died, the one who eats this bread will live forever.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people in the synagogue at Capernaum.
He said, “This bread came down from heaven.
Your fathers ate manna in the wilderness.
They died.
This bread is not like that manna.
Anyone who eats this bread will live forever.”
passages.original: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἄρτος ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καταβάς οὐ καθὼς ἔφαγον οἱ πατέρες καὶ ἀπέθανον ὁ τρώγων τοῦτον τὸν ἄρτον ζήσει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα

passages.text: Jesus said this while teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke these words.\r\nHe taught in the synagogue.\r\nHe was in Capernaum.
passages.original: Ταῦτα εἶπεν ἐν συναγωγῇ διδάσκων ἐν Καφαρναούμ

passages.text: On hearing it, many of His disciples said, “This is a difficult teaching. Who can accept it?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus taught in the synagogue at Capernaum.
Many of His disciples listened to His words.
They heard His teaching about the bread from heaven.
Many disciples said, “This teaching is difficult.”
They asked, “Who can accept this?”
passages.original: Πολλοὶ οὖν ἀκούσαντες ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ εἶπαν Σκληρός ἐστιν ὁ λόγος οὗτος τίς δύναται αὐτοῦ ἀκούειν

passages.text: Aware that His disciples were grumbling about this teaching, Jesus asked them, “Does this offend you?
passages.sermon:
Jesus was teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum.
Jesus knew what His disciples were thinking.
His disciples were grumbling about His teaching.
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus asked, “Does this offend you?”
passages.original: Εἰδὼς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν ἑαυτῷ ὅτι γογγύζουσιν περὶ τούτου οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τοῦτο ὑμᾶς σκανδαλίζει

passages.text: Then what will happen if you see the Son of Man ascend to where He was before?
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus once lived in heaven before coming to earth.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “What will you do if you see the Son of Man go up to where He was before?”
passages.original: ἐὰν οὖν θεωρῆτε τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀναβαίνοντα ὅπου ἦν τὸ πρότερον

passages.text: The Spirit gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and they are life.
passages.sermon:
The Spirit gives life.
The flesh gives nothing good.
My words are spirit.
My words are life.
passages.original: Τὸ πνεῦμά ἐστιν τὸ ζωοποιοῦν ἡ σὰρξ οὐκ ὠφελεῖ οὐδέν τὰ ῥήματα ἃ ἐγὼ λελάληκα ὑμῖν πνεῦμά ἐστιν καὶ ζωή ἐστιν

passages.text: However, there are some of you who do not believe.” (For Jesus had known from the beginning which of them did not believe and who would betray Him.)
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Some people among you do not believe.
Jesus knew this from the beginning.
Jesus knew which people did not believe.
Jesus also knew who would betray Him.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ εἰσὶν ἐξ ὑμῶν τινες οἳ οὐ πιστεύουσιν ᾔδει γὰρ ἐξ ἀρχῆς ὁ Ἰησοῦς τίνες εἰσὶν οἱ μὴ πιστεύοντες καὶ τίς ἐστιν ὁ παραδώσων αὐτόν

passages.text: Then Jesus said, “This is why I told you that no one can come to Me unless the Father has granted it to him.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus explained an important truth.
No one can come to Jesus by their own power.
The Father must give permission for someone to come to Jesus.
Only those whom the Father grants can come to Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν Διὰ τοῦτο εἴρηκα ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς δύναται ἐλθεῖν πρός με ἐὰν μὴ ᾖ δεδομένον αὐτῷ ἐκ τοῦ Πατρός

passages.text: From that time on many of His disciples turned back and no longer walked with Him.
passages.sermon:
Many people followed Jesus.
Some of these people were called His disciples.
From that time, many of His disciples turned back.
They stopped following Jesus.
They no longer walked with Him.
passages.original: Ἐκ τούτου πολλοὶ ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἀπῆλθον εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω καὶ οὐκέτι μετ’ αὐτοῦ περιεπάτουν

passages.text: So Jesus asked the Twelve, “Do you want to leave too?”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the Twelve disciples.\r\nHe asked them a question.\r\nHe said, “Do you also want to leave?”
passages.original: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς δώδεκα Μὴ καὶ ὑμεῖς θέλετε ὑπάγειν

passages.text: Simon Peter replied, “Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life.
passages.sermon:
Simon Peter was one of the Twelve disciples of Jesus.
Simon Peter replied to Jesus.
Simon Peter said, “Lord, to whom would we go?”
Simon Peter said, “You have the words of eternal life.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ Σίμων Πέτρος Κύριε πρὸς τίνα ἀπελευσόμεθα ῥήματα ζωῆς αἰωνίου ἔχεις

passages.text: We believe and know that You are the Holy One of God.”
passages.sermon:
Simon Peter spoke to Jesus.
Simon Peter and the other disciples believed Jesus.
Simon Peter and the other disciples knew Jesus.
Jesus is the Holy One of God.
passages.original: καὶ ἡμεῖς πεπιστεύκαμεν καὶ ἐγνώκαμεν ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ Ἅγιος τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Jesus answered them, “Have I not chosen you, the Twelve? Yet one of you is a devil!”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the twelve disciples.\r\nJesus said, "I chose you, the Twelve."\r\nOne of you is a devil.
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐκ ἐγὼ ὑμᾶς τοὺς δώδεκα ἐξελεξάμην καὶ ἐξ ὑμῶν εἷς διάβολός ἐστιν

passages.text: He was speaking about Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot. For although Judas was one of the Twelve, he was later to betray Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about Judas.
Judas was the son of Simon Iscariot.
Judas was one of the Twelve disciples.
Judas would later betray Jesus.
passages.original: ἔλεγεν δὲ τὸν Ἰούδαν Σίμωνος Ἰσκαριώτου οὗτος γὰρ ἔμελλεν παραδιδόναι αὐτόν εἷς ἐκ τῶν δώδεκα
